question_text:
That the dyers of the Ombrisk coast soaked their wool skeins in fermented bark liquor before mordanting them not only explains the unusual depth of the surviving reds but also ______ why later workshops, working from the same written recipes, failed to match the colors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The convention being tested is subject-verb agreement within a compound predicate. The subject of the sentence is the entire noun clause "That the dyers ... mordanting them," and a noun clause used as a subject is singular. The correlative pair "not only ... but also" joins two verbs that share this subject, so the second verb, like the first verb "explains," must be a singular present-tense verb. "Clarifies" is that verb.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect because the plural verb "clarify" doesn't agree in number with the subject. The plural nouns "reds" and "skeins" are tempting, but the subject is the singular noun clause beginning with "That," which is also the subject of the singular verb "explains."
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect because "not only ... but also" joins two parallel predicates, and the first, "explains," is present tense. The past tense "clarified" breaks that parallelism. The past tense "failed" belongs to the separate clause beginning with "why" and doesn't govern this verb.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect because the nonfinite form "clarifying" can't function as a main verb. The pair "not only ... but also" requires the second element to match the first, the finite verb "explains," so the sentence needs a finite verb in the blank.

question_text:
Surveyors who toured the Ternvale uplands in 1861 noted that nearly every longhouse there had a steeply pitched roof with deep, overhanging eaves. That heavy snow slid off those roofs and away from the timber walls ______ among the chief reasons the uplanders had abandoned flat roofs in the 1790s.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The convention being tested is subject-verb agreement. The subject of the second sentence is the entire noun clause "That heavy snow slid off those roofs and away from the timber walls," in which "That" is a conjunction introducing a noun clause, not a demonstrative modifying "snow." This clause names a single idea and therefore takes a singular verb, even though the plural noun "walls" comes right before the blank and the plural noun "reasons" follows it. The singular past-tense "was" agrees with this subject and fits the text's past time frame.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect because the plural verb "were" doesn't agree in number with the singular subject. A verb agrees with its subject, not with the plural noun "walls" before the blank or the plural noun "reasons" after it, and the subject here is a singular noun clause.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect because the plural verb "are" doesn't agree in number with the singular noun-clause subject "That heavy snow slid off those roofs and away from the timber walls." The plural nouns near the blank don't determine the verb's number. The present tense "are" also clashes with the text's past time frame.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect because the plural verb "have been" doesn't agree in number with the singular noun-clause subject. The plural noun "walls" before the blank and the plural noun "reasons" after it don't determine the verb's number. The present perfect also doesn't fit a reason for a decision completed in the 1790s.
